papers.title: Machine Learning Methods for Automatic Sleep Stage Classification: Current Status and Future Challenges.
papers.summary: Reviews machine learning methods for automatic sleep stage classification, covering the full pipeline from data collection devices through feature extraction and selection to single-, dual-, and multi-modality classifiers, and outlines challenges and future directions with emphasis on lightweight home-use monitoring.

papers.title: GamSleepNet: A Lightweight Automatic Sleep Staging Framework Based on Gabor Feature Extraction and Mamba Sequence Modeling for Single-Channel EEG.
papers.summary: Proposed GamSleepNet, a lightweight single-channel EEG sleep-staging framework combining improved Gabor feature extraction with a learnable filter branch and a Mamba selective state-space model, plus teacher-student feature alignment and two-stage training. On Sleep-EDF it reached 87.86% accuracy and 82.62% macro-F1 with only 30.86k parameters, improving recognition of difficult N1 and REM stages and remaining stable under low SNR and label scarcity.

papers.title: A Temporally Causal Two-Layer Framework for Wearable EEG Sleep Staging and Short-Horizon Sleep-Transition Forecasting.
papers.summary: Developed a temporally causal two-layer framework for wearable EEG in which a five-stage sleep classifier (M0) fed cross-fitted stage-probability histories to a second layer (M1) forecasting transitions from wake/N1 to N2/N3/REM within 60-120 s. M0 achieved 0.830 accuracy and 0.704 macro-F1, and M1 reached AUROC 0.801, 0.791, and 0.786 at 60, 90, and 120 s respectively, with cross-device limitations identified on Muse S Gen2 recordings.

papers.title: Identification of Insomnia Disorder Using Machine Learning and Wearable Technology.
papers.summary: Used overnight forehead wearable EEG with five machine learning models to classify 112 insomnia disorder patients versus 98 healthy controls; CatBoost models including periodic features reached the highest AUC (0.765), and SHAP ranked delta-band power and sleep timing as top contributors.

papers.title: MG-STNet: A Compact Multi-Granularity Spatiotemporal Network for Adaptive Sleep Staging.
papers.summary: Proposed MG-STNet, a compact multi-granularity spatiotemporal network for sleep staging using parallel downsampling branches, global-local feature recalibration, adaptive spatiotemporal convolution, and temporal attention encoding. On Sleep-EDF-20 and Sleep-EDF-78 it achieved 87.3% and 84.5% accuracy (four-channel, 46.6K parameters) and 86.6% and 83.2% (single-channel), offering a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

papers.title: Operational Definitions of Transition Onset Shape EEG Biomarker Timing in Drowsiness: A Single-Channel Method Comparison.
papers.summary: Built a benchmarking framework to test how operational definitions of transition onset affect EEG drowsiness lead-time claims, applying seven onset estimators and 32 single-channel frontal EEG features across 17 participants with replication in DROZY. Estimator choice shifted onsets by minutes and detection coverage ranged from 45% to 100%, while no estimator showed excess pre-anchor onsets versus surrogate data, prompting proposed interpretability criteria, evidence levels, and a reporting checklist.

papers.title: Pre-anaesthetic anxiety phenotype stratifies anaesthesia EEG, acquired navigation, and post-anaesthesia sleep in sevoflurane-exposed mice
papers.summary: Classified 42 mice as low- or high-anxiety by fear-retrieval freezing and exposed them to sevoflurane without surgery; high-anxiety mice showed higher aperiodic spectral edge frequency at adequate anaesthesia, selectively disrupted learned navigation sequences, and decreased REM sleep, indicating that pre-anaesthetic anxiety phenotype tracks multiple anaesthesia responses.

papers.title: Compact SC-LIF: A factorized hybrid network for motor imagery EEG decoding.
papers.summary: Develops Compact SC-LIF, a factorized temporal-spatial convolutional spike-count LIF network for motor imagery EEG decoding, achieving 71.91% subject-level accuracy and 71.72% macro-F1 with 3,508 parameters and 6.45 million dense synaptic MACs per trial, with gains of 8.24-10.10 percentage points over several baselines and a 29.0% operation reduction attributed to front-end factorization.

papers.title: Sparse EEG neurodynamics of hypoglycemia in type 1 diabetes with personal euglycemic baseline adaptation.
papers.summary: Benchmarked 24 EEG models under leave-one-subject-out validation for hypoglycemia detection in type 1 diabetes and applied Personal Euglycemic Baseline Adaptation (PEBA); PEBA raised balanced accuracy (e.g., 0.68 to 0.83 for feature-domain Sinc-SSNET) while channel/feature sparsification cut parameters by 88.51%-99.88% with the F7 log-theta descriptor increasing during hypoglycemia in 88.2% of participants.

papers.title: AI-Driven Non-Invasive Scalp EEG Biosensing for Real-Time Seizure Prediction Using Lightweight Gradient Boosting Ensembles.
papers.summary: Developed a computationally lightweight, patient-independent machine learning pipeline using an ensemble of regularized XGBoost and LightGBM on CHB-MIT scalp EEG, and on four completely unseen subjects achieved 100% event-level seizure sensitivity (34/34) with a false alarm rate of 0.415/h and a mean prediction horizon of 17.03 min at 0.0057 ms per window.

papers.title: Scalp EEG seizure warning in children under a pre-specified, locked evaluation: confound audit, structured chance levels and a negative result
papers.summary: Evaluated scalp EEG seizure warning in 21 monitored children under a pre-specified, locked protocol, finding the initial method (44% of seizures, 0.48 false alarms/hour) no better than chance. A redesigned state-conditioned scheme achieved 33% detection during cross-validation but failed to exceed structured chance in two external validation cohorts (19% detection at 0.60 false alarms/hour versus 26% chance), a negative result.

papers.title: DualBranchEEG: A Dual-Branch CNN BiLSTM Network with Temporal Attention and Spectral Features for Three Class EEG Seizure Classification
papers.summary: Presents DualBranchEEG, a dual-branch CNN-BiLSTM with temporal attention fused with Welch log-power spectral features, for three-class seizure classification on the Bonn EEG dataset; the full model reached 96.00% test accuracy, macro F1 0.9543, and macro AUC-ROC 0.9952, comparable to a CNN-BiLSTM baseline that achieved 98.40% accuracy under five-fold cross-validation.

papers.title: Objective-to-Subjective Sleep Discrepancy in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Pilot EEG Study.
papers.summary: In a pilot study of 22 hospitalized rheumatoid arthritis patients using portable single-channel EEG, subjective total sleep time exceeded EEG-derived TST by a median of 82.75 min and was uncorrelated with it, with a more positive discrepancy associated with lower albumin, higher CRP, glucocorticoid use, higher DAS28-CRP, and functional disability.

papers.title: Cognitive load detection using hyper-learning dragonfly optimization for feature selection.
papers.summary: Proposes an EEG-based cognitive load detection framework combining empirical Fourier decomposition, entropy-based feature extraction, and hyper-learning binary dragonfly feature selection (HLBDA), classified with KNN/ensemble subspace KNN. Achieved accuracies of 97.13%, 96.48%, and 98.2% on MAT, STEW, and MLR datasets, with the frontal lobe showing the strongest lobe-wise discriminative capability.

papers.title: Source-reconstructed EEG graph signal processing: Pitfalls and workarounds.
papers.summary: Investigated methodological biases in source-reconstructed EEG graph signal processing, showing that uncorrected SVD polarity ambiguity inflates high-frequency graph power (mitigated by a proposed sign-control method) and that electrical source imaging spatial leakage inflates low-frequency content, with stronger effects during spikes and for eLORETA and Euclidean-distance connectomes.

papers.title: Automated Interictal Epileptiform Discharge Detector Scores in Serial EEG: Record-Level Concordance Did Not Extend to Within-Participant Change.
papers.summary: Secondary analysis of serial EEG from 15 adults with drug-resistant focal epilepsy tested concordance among three pretrained automated interictal epileptiform discharge detectors. Record-level correlations (ρ=0.341 to 0.696) did not extend to within-participant change scores, which were smaller and nonsignificant after Holm adjustment, with limited directional agreement.

papers.title: Case Report: Clinical applications of extended-duration remote ambulatory EEG monitoring: lessons from real-world cases.
papers.summary: Presents clinical utility frameworks and three real-world case studies using the REMI wireless wearable 4-sensor remote ambulatory EEG system with cloud transmission and AI seizure detection. Extended-duration monitoring (up to 30 days) captured seizures beyond the standard 72-h window in one case, ruled out electrographic seizures in another, and guided treatment in a third.

papers.title: Frequency-embedded sequence learning for multi-class EEG-to-text interface.
papers.summary: Proposed a lightweight 1D-CNN pipeline for 5-class EEG-to-text decoding trained on time-domain EEG versus frequency-embedded PSD sequences, reaching mean intra-subject accuracies of 46.1% and 64.4% respectively (peaks 54% and 82%), while inter-subject pooled performance remained near chance (~23-25%).

papers.title: Cross-subject EEG emotion recognition network based on moment channel attention.
papers.summary: Proposes MAC-ETN, a hybrid Moment Channel Attention and Transformer network for cross-subject EEG emotion recognition, evaluated on DEAP and MAHNOB-HCI with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. The model's main advantage was markedly reduced cross-subject performance variability (lowest accuracy standard deviations among compared methods) rather than higher mean accuracy (61.26% arousal, 60.47% valence on DEAP).

papers.title: Dynamic mesh pattern-based substance use addiction detection from EEG signals.
papers.summary: Presents an explainable EEG framework, Dynamic Mesh Pattern with explainable feature engineering (DynMeshPat-XFE) combined with CWNCA, tkNN, and Directed Lobish, to distinguish substance use disorder from controls. On 1985 EEG segments from 60 participants using leave-one-subject-out CV, the 22-column model achieved 99.45% segment-level accuracy, rising to 99.70% after excluding channels A1, A2, and E.

papers.title: EEG Theta Power as an Indicator of Cognitive Workload in Student Pilots.
papers.summary: Measured scalp EEG theta (4-8 Hz) power at eight locations in ten student pilots during baseline and three high-fidelity PC-21 flight simulator modules of differing difficulty, with NASA-TLX workload ratings after each phase. Theta power was higher in the most cognitively demanding phase across frontal, temporal, and occipital regions, but correlations between theta measures and subjective workload ratings were weak and inconsistent at the group level.

papers.title: Age-Adjusted Exploratory Analysis of Spectral, Aperiodic, and Microstate Electroencephalography Features in Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.summary: Examined age-adjusted associations between resting-state EEG spectral, aperiodic, and microstate features and multiple sclerosis in the BrainLat dataset (32 MS, 32 controls). After FDR correction, global bandwidth, global aperiodic offset, and channel-wise aperiodic offset were significantly associated with diagnosis, whereas central frequency, exponent, power spectral density, and all microstate measures were not; the non-overlapping age ranges limit interpretation.

papers.title: Predicting Seizure Recurrence After Withdrawal of Antiseizure Medications Through Electroencephalogram Connectivity Analysis: A Proof-of-Concept Study.
papers.summary: Applied EEG connectivity analysis using directed transfer function (DTF) to predict seizure recurrence after antiseizure medication withdrawal in 63 patients (29 recurrence, 34 nonrecurrence). Found significantly higher DTF connectivity in motor regions (BA4, BA6) in the recurrence group, and a SVM classifier using 16 DTF features achieved 93.36% accuracy (sensitivity 96.67%, specificity 90.58%, AUC 93.63%).

papers.title: Physiology-Guided Spiking Neural Networks for EEG Motor-Imagery Recognition.
papers.summary: Introduces PG-SNN, a spiking neural network that embeds sensorimotor physiological priors into event coding, electrode-prior graph spatial propagation, and multi-timescale spike dynamics for motor-imagery EEG decoding. It reached 84.72% accuracy (kappa 0.796) on BCI Competition IV-2a and 71.28% (kappa 0.617) on EEGMMIDB, exceeding matched ANN and SNN baselines.

papers.title: Multicentre electrophysiology reveals the limits of auditory prediction responses as biomarkers of chronic tinnitus
papers.summary: Investigated auditory prediction responses as biomarkers of chronic tinnitus using EEG in 440 adults (226 with tinnitus, 214 without) across six centres. Found that most electrophysiological group differences were attenuated after adjusting for demographic and audiological factors, and classification based on EEG features achieved cross-validated AUC of 0.624 (0.689 with demographic/audiological predictors) but limited predictive value for tinnitus burden or loudness.

papers.title: Intraoperative Subcallosal Cingulate Local Field Potential Spectral Analysis During Emotion-Evoking Music in Treatment-Resistant Depression With Multitarget Deep Brain Stimulation: A Case Report.
papers.summary: Reported a case of intraoperative subcallosal cingulate local field potential recordings during emotion-evoking music in a patient with treatment-resistant depression undergoing multitarget deep brain stimulation. After excluding artifacts, broadband power relative to baseline was higher during a sad song than during a happy song (p=0.024), and depression and anxiety scores improved at three months; the authors emphasize the need for artifact control in such recordings.

papers.title: Brain rhythms during Instagram Reels viewing and subsequent performance on sustained attention and working memory: an EEG study
papers.summary: Examined the effects of 10 minutes of Instagram Reels viewing on EEG activity, sustained attention, and working memory in 30 university students using a counterbalanced within-subject design. Found higher posterior relative theta power and lower alpha-to-theta ratio during Reels viewing compared to neutral images, but no significant differences in attention or working-memory performance after correction for multiple comparisons.

papers.title: Sensorimotor EEG Responses and Parietal Symmetry Objectively Reflect Ankle Kinesthesia and Position Sense in Healthy Middle-Aged and Older Adults.
papers.summary: Combined joint position reproduction and passive movement detection with EEG in 15 healthy middle-aged and older adults to examine cortical correlates of ankle position sense and kinesthesia. Lower parietal brain symmetry index was associated with smaller position matching error, and movement-evoked N1 latency was positively associated with movement detection time, providing physiological references for ankle proprioception.

papers.title: Development and Evaluation of a Cap-Mounted Tripolar Concentric Ring Electrode System with a Central Gel-Delivery Opening for tEEG and EEG Recording.
papers.summary: Developed a gold-plated copper tripolar concentric ring electrode with a 2 mm central gel-delivery opening and 3D-printed cap-mounted holder, and evaluated it in ten healthy adults at occipital hair-bearing sites. The system recorded identifiable VEPs (peaks near 105 and 141 ms), eEEG VEPs at O1/O2 strongly correlated with Pz (median r=0.897 and 0.938), and alpha power increased significantly with eye closure in gel-coupled tEEG channels (Holm-adjusted p=0.0195).

papers.title: Quantitative EEG Differences Across Two Sedation Conditions in a Child with Epilepsy: A Case Report.
papers.summary: A within-subject case report compared quantitative interictal EEG in a child with congenital CMV-associated structural epilepsy under propofol versus chloral hydrate sedation using duration-matched 15.52-min segments. The chloral hydrate recording showed higher spike frequency (14.11 vs. 4.12 spikes/min; rate ratio 3.42) and spike index (84.95% vs. 27.96%), with lower SEF95 and greater delta predominance under propofol, though recordings occurred about a year apart and differences cannot be attributed specifically to the sedatives.

papers.title: Acute Effects of Prolonged Intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation on Cortical Excitability: A Randomized Crossover TMS-EEG Study
papers.summary: In a randomized, sham-controlled crossover TMS-EEG trial in 40 healthy males, a single session of prolonged intermittent theta burst stimulation over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex modulated left frontal theta power between stimulation trains, while pre-to-post TMS-evoked potentials and behavioral outcomes did not differ between active and sham conditions.

papers.title: Hybrid EEG-EOG Brain-Computer Interface for Virtual-Reality Powered Mobility Training in Children with Severe Neuromotor Disabilities: A Multiple-Case Feasibility Study.
papers.summary: Multiple-case feasibility study of a hybrid EEG-EOG brain-computer interface integrated with a virtual reality powered wheelchair simulator in six children and adolescents with severe neuromotor disabilities, using kinesthetic motor imagery for steering and EOG blinks for discrete commands. Mean online classification accuracy was 67% (77% in successful evaluations), four participants completed the protocol, and workload and VR tolerability were acceptable.

papers.title: From hemodynamics to function: the role of fNIRS and hybrid EEG-fNIRS systems in next-generation assistive technologies for rehabilitation.
papers.summary: Systematically reviewed the evolution of assistive technology control modalities and the technical capabilities and limitations of fNIRS and hybrid EEG-fNIRS systems for rehabilitation and brain-computer interfaces. Concludes that hybrid EEG-fNIRS combines high temporal with spatial/hemodynamic information to improve accuracy and adaptability toward more user-centered rehabilitation technologies.

papers.title: Differential Neurophysiological Signatures of Asymptomatic Carotid and Intracranial Atherosclerotic Stenosis: A Multimodal Resting-State EEG Study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional multimodal resting-state EEG study of 68 participants, asymptomatic carotid stenosis and asymptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis showed shared reductions in microstate A coverage and A-to-C transitions, but ACS additionally had shortened MsA duration, reduced alpha power, and increased alpha-band connectivity within a distributed NBS network, whereas aICAS showed increased B–D microstate transitions without a significant NBS component. Selected microstate measures remained associated with Trail Making Test performance and yielded moderate cross-validated ROC discrimination (AUC 0.675–0.744).

papers.title: A case of dissociative disorder with attenuation of EEG alpha power during a depersonalization episode.
papers.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
papers.summary: This case report describes an adolescent female with a dissociative disorder whose 24-h video-EEG monitoring captured a transient widespread reduction in alpha power coinciding with a depersonalization episode, despite no findings supporting epilepsy.

papers.title: EEG morphology and peri-ictal MRI abnormalities in status epilepticus and ictal-interictal continuum.
papers.summary: In a single-center prospective cohort of 205 patients with status epilepticus or ictal-interictal continuum, excitatory-predominant EEG morphology and lateralized periodic discharges were associated with increased risk of peri-ictal DWI/FLAIR MRI abnormalities, with excitatory feature count correlating with the extent of affected MRI sequences.

papers.title: Cognition in 6-17-year-olds with Generalized and Focal Pharmaco-responsive Non-structural Epilepsies and its Correlates on Diffusion Tensor Imaging and Quantitative EEG: A Comparative Observational Study.
papers.summary: In a comparative observational study of 20 generalized and 30 focal pharmaco-responsive non-structural pediatric epilepsies, cognition was similarly impaired in both groups versus historical controls and correlated with corpus callosum and cingulate fractional anisotropy on DTI plus several qEEG power measures.

papers.title: Changes in Clinical Management Related to Continuous Versus Routine Electroencephalogram in Critically Ill Adults: Analysis of a Randomized Trial.
papers.summary: This ancillary analysis of the randomized CERTA trial compared continuous versus repeated routine EEG in 364 critically ill adults with altered consciousness and found more clinical management changes with cEEG (58.2% vs 45.6%, p=0.018), driven mainly by anti-seizure medication modification (22.0% vs 12.1%, p=0.012). After adjusting for ASM modifications, 6-month mortality and functional outcome remained similar between EEG groups, indicating that increased management changes did not translate into improved outcomes.

papers.title: The utility of additional electrodes during stereo-electroencephalography for pediatric epilepsy surgery.
papers.summary: In a retrospective pediatric cohort of 14 patients, additional SEEG electrode placement during the same hospitalization was well tolerated with few minor complications and helped refine surgical margins or resolve inconclusive localization, with 75% of operated patients reaching ILAE 1-3 at latest follow-up.

papers.title: Correction: Multimodal EEG and explainable machine learning characterize neuroticism-related neurodynamic heterogeneity in mild cognitive impairment during visuospatial working memory.
papers.summary: Published erratum correcting a prior article on multimodal EEG and explainable machine learning used to characterize neuroticism-related neurodynamic heterogeneity in mild cognitive impairment during visuospatial working memory; no original findings are reported in this correction notice.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
